classes.description: Emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil (Truvada and generics), emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (Descovy), cabotegravir LA (Apretude), lenacapavir (Yeztugo).
classes.plainDescription: A daily pill or long-acting shot that prevents HIV.

classes.plainDescription: A once-a-day pill that treats HIV.

Every complete single-tablet regimen on the PDL carries Auto PA, so the pick is Biktarvy, the most commonly written option in the class. Efavirenz-based generics are on the PDL but are older, less preferred regimens, so not picked. Complera, Delstrigo and efavirenz/lamivudine/TDF are complete regimens and are included under the class's 'complete single-tablet' wording. Not on PDL: none additional; Cabenuva listed here as a PA item.

records.verificationNote: Biktarvy 50/200/25 mg tablet read on page 39: Tier 5 (DL), QL 30 per 30 days, no PA. Judgment call: the generic efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF tablet (Tier 4, no PA) is the lower-tier option, but the efavirenz regimen is an older choice than the integrase-based single tablets, so Biktarvy is picked; a reviewer should confirm. DL (Dispensing Limit) means a 30-day supply limit per page 10. Triumeq PD (pediatric) is excluded. Stribild and Delstrigo are listed on page 39-41 but are not named in this class. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: Re-read by x-coordinate on v17 page 39. Adjudicated: Biktarvy (Tier 5, DL, QL 30 per 30 days, no PA) kept as the pick: integrase-based single tablets are the current first-line choice and none of the lower-tier options is an equivalent single-tablet regimen (generic efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is Tier 4). Specialty-tier drugs are not eligible for tiering exceptions.]
